title: Sidebar: Add status-based filtering with refactored status architecture
description:
Closes https://github.com/storybookjs/storybook/issues/34302

<!-- If your PR is related to an issue, provide the number(s) above; if it resolves multiple issues, be sure to break them up (e.g. "closes #1000, closes #1001"). -->

<!--

Thank you for contributing to Storybook! Please submit all PRs to the `next` branch unless they are specific to the current release. Storybook maintainers cherry-pick bug and documentation fixes into the `main` branch as part of the release process, so you shouldn't need to worry about this. For additional guidance: https://storybook.js.org/docs/contribute

-->

## What I did

- Added status-based filtering to the sidebar, allowing users to filter stories by status values (new, modified, affected, error, warning, success, pending, unknown) alongside existing tag-based filtering
- Refactored `getStatus` in `status.tsx` from returning tuples to returning named objects (`{ icon, iconColor, textColor }`), making it the single source of truth for both icon colors and text colors
- `StatusButton.tsx`'s `withStatusColor` now delegates to `getStatus` instead of maintaining a separate color mapping
- Restructured `FilterPanel` for better separation of concerns:
  - `FilterPanel.utils.ts` — constants, types, and pure utility functions
  - `FilterPanelItem.tsx` — individual filter row rendering
  - `useFilterData.tsx` — data hooks (`useTagFilterItems`, `useStatusFilterItems`)
  - `FilterPanel.tsx` — thin orchestrator component
- Renamed `TagsFilter` → `Filter` and `TagsFilterPanel` → `FilterPanel` to reflect the broader filtering scope
- Added new status icon symbols (new, modified, affected) to `IconSymbols.tsx`
- Extended manager API with `addStatusFilters`, `removeStatusFilters`, `resetStatusFilters`, and `setAllTagFilters` methods
- Added comprehensive tests for status utilities and stories module

human_comments.body:
_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟡 Minor_

**`makeStatuses` drops earlier statuses for duplicate `storyId`s.**

Line 213 currently rebuilds each `storyId` entry from scratch, so if two values use the same `storyId`, the later one overwrites the previous `typeId` map. This can silently hide statuses in composed fixtures.

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
 const makeStatuses = (
   ...values: Array<{ storyId: string; typeId: string; statusValue: StatusValue; title: string }>
 ): StatusesByStoryIdAndTypeId =>
-  Object.fromEntries(
-    values.map(({ storyId, typeId, statusValue, title }) => [
-      storyId,
-      {
-        [typeId]: {
-          value: statusValue,
-          typeId,
-          storyId,
-          title,
-          description: '',
-        },
-      },
-    ])
-  );
+  values.reduce<StatusesByStoryIdAndTypeId>((acc, { storyId, typeId, statusValue, title }) => {
+    acc[storyId] ??= {};
+    acc[storyId][typeId] = {
+      value: statusValue,
+      typeId,
+      storyId,
+      title,
+      description: '',
+    };
+    return acc;
+  }, {});
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed.

In `@code/core/src/manager/components/sidebar/FilterPanel.stories.tsx` around
lines 213 - 225, The current makeStatuses construction using Object.fromEntries
over values rebuilds each storyId entry and overwrites previous typeId maps when
duplicate storyId appears; change makeStatuses to accumulate/merge entries
instead (e.g., use values.reduce or a Map) so for each item (referencing
storyId, typeId, statusValue, title) you check if an entry for that storyId
already exists and then add/merge the new typeId object into the existing map
rather than replacing it, ensuring description/title/statusValue are set for the
new typeId while preserving any previously added typeIds for that same storyId.
```

</details>
